### `discussionboard_moderation_action`

Moderation Actions - This implements the moderation action tracking requirement from the Functional Requirements and Business Rules documents, specifically for documenting all interventions by moderators or admins.

Records every moderation event (edit, hide, delete, warn, ban, restore, etc.) performed on posts, comments, or user accounts to ensure a complete audit trail. Maintains 3NF compliance by splitting the core action event from any additional notes or ban details (captured in related tables). For example, each time a moderator deletes or edits a post, an action is recorded here.

Key relationships: Links to the acting moderator/admin, the target user (if applicable), the affected post/comment, and the report triggering this action (if present).
Special behaviors: Enforces normalized structure; only atomic, non-derived data allowed. Relies on foreign keys for relating to users, posts, comments, and reports. No duplication of action details; rich detail via relation tables.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key - Unique identifier for each moderation action record. Implements uniqueness and normalized referencing as required by 3NF. For example, used to retrieve or cross-reference specific moderation activities.
- `actor_moderator_id`: Actor Moderator/Admin - References the user (moderator/admin) performing the action. Implements responsibility traceability requirement from moderation rules. Ensures normalized, non-redundant representation with atomic foreign key. For example, used to determine which moderator enforced a ban or edited a post.
- `target_user_id`: Target User - References the user affected by this moderation action, if applicable (e.g., ban, warning). Implements business auditability and precise incident mapping. Nullable because not all actions target a user (e.g., post deletion may not specify a user directly).
- `post_id`: Affected Post - Optionally links to the post affected by this moderation action. Implements requirement for direct content-moderation tracking. Nullable as not all actions affect posts (could affect comments or users only).
- `comment_id`: Affected Comment - Optionally links to the comment affected by the moderation action. Ensures content-level traceability. Nullable since some actions may not involve comments.
- `report_id`: Linked Report - Optionally associates this action with a triggering user report. Fulfills requirement for moderation workflow traceability. Nullable if the action was not prompted by a report (e.g., proactive moderation).
- `action_type`: Type of Moderation Action - Implements the audit logging requirement. Business meaning: which kind of moderation was done (e.g., 'edit', 'delete', 'warn', 'ban', 'restore'). Ensures normalization by storing a single action type per event. For example, 'ban' when a user is banned.
- `action_reason`: Moderation Reason/Note - Documents the reason for this moderation action. Implements the business traceability requirement from reporting and audit logging rules. Ensures normalization by keeping rationale separate from user and content records. For example, 'Spam detected' or 'Offensive language'.
- `created_at`: Moderation Action Timestamp - Records when the moderation action was performed. Implements audit logging and recovery requirement. Maintains normalization as every action gets a single timestamp.

### `discussionboard_ban`

User Ban Records - Implements the ban/timeout handling requirements from the Moderation Features and Business Rules. 

Maintains a normalized, atomic record of each user ban, with duration, moderator, and reasons stored independently for robust traceability. Strictly normalized (3NF), all ban details are atomic, with external links to users and the moderating actor. Example: each time a user is banned (temporary or permanent), a distinct record captures specifics.

Key relationships: Links to the affected user, imposing moderator/admin, and the associated moderation action (for logic traceability).
Special behaviors: Prohibits redundancy; if ban is lifted/restored, a separate moderation action is created and linked in the action table.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key - Unique identifier for the ban record. Required for normalized, referenceable ban tracking.
- `user_id`: Banned User - Reference to the user being banned. Implements business rule for precise accountability. Atomic, normalized field. For example, used to display active bans for a user.
- `moderator_id`: Imposing Moderator/Admin - Reference to the moderator/admin that imposed the ban. Implements responsibility traceability. Normalized, non-redundant. For example, used in reporting patterns in moderation activity.
- `moderation_action_id`: Related Moderation Action - Links this ban to the underlying moderation action that initiated it. Fulfills normalized structure and audit trail requirements. For example, cross-references why and how the ban was imposed.
- `start_at`: Ban Start Timestamp - When the ban/timeout begins. Implements requirement for precise timing. Maintains normalization by only representing the atomic start date/time.
- `end_at`: Ban End Timestamp - When the ban/timeout ends (nullable for permanent bans). Implements normalized design by allowing indefinite bans (null end date). For example, set to null for permanent bans.
- `ban_reason`: Ban Reason - Human-readable reason for ban. Implements auditability requirement. Normalized, atomic field. Example: 'Repeated rule violation'.

### `discussionboard_moderator_note`

Moderator System Notes - Implements the system-logged note-taking requirements from the Moderation Features section in Functional Requirements and Business Rules.

Maintains atomic, normalized moderator notes about specific actions, users, or incidents for future reference or compliance. Each note is linked to its author (moderator/admin) and can be associated with any related moderation action or user, upholding 3NF by splitting extra narrative/context data from core event/action records. Example: a moderator leaves an internal explanation for why a complex decision was made.

Key relationships: Links to the authoring moderator, optionally to a user or moderation action. Can be used for system auditing or internal collaboration.
Special behaviors: Multiple notes per action/user permitted. Cannot directly trigger external changes, only stores commentary or rationale.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key - Unique note identifier. Implements normalized storage per note instance.
- `author_id`: Author Moderator/Admin - The user (moderator/admin) writing the note.  Implements traceability and accountability requirements. For example, used in reports to show note authorship.
- `related_action_id`: Related Moderation Action - Optionally links a note to a specific moderation action (if applicable). Implements auditability and contextual requirements for notes about actions. Nullable, as not all notes relate to a particular action.
- `target_user_id`: Target User - Optionally links a note to a particular user (e.g., as rationale for ongoing watchlist status). Implements traceability for user-centric notes. Nullable; note can be general or related to action only.
- `note_body`: Note Body - The content of the system note. Implements audit/compliance requirements and internal communication needs. Maintains atomic, normalized storage per note instance. For example, describes decision rationale.
- `created_at`: Creation Timestamp - When the note was authored. Implements audit/trace requirements. Normalized since each note has exactly one creation timestamp.

### `discussionboard_notification`

[Notification record] - This implements the user notification delivery requirement from the functional requirements (Section 7, Notifications & User Engagement).

Stores individual notification events delivered or pending for users. Each row records a specific notification destined for a user, including what triggered it (reply, like, mention, report resolution), the related entities (such as post/comment/report), and the unread/read status. This supports granular alert delivery and tracking.

Maintains 3NF compliance by:
- Referencing related entities via foreign keys only (no denormalized summary fields)
- All notification metadata is atomic (type, status, timestamps, actor)

For example, a user receives a notification when someone replies to their post. This record contains which user, which post, what type of event, and whether it was read.

Key relationships: references user, optional links to post/comment/report.
Special behaviors: notifications are marked as read/unread; purged after retention period if needed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`
  > [Primary key] - Implements requirement for unique notification identification.
  >
  > Uniquely identifies this notification record in the system. Ensures normalization as every notification is atomic and unambiguous. Used for queries, updates, and deletion.
- `user_id`
  > [Notification recipient] - Implements the requirement to deliver notifications to specific users.
  >
  > Links this notification to the recipient user. Ensures 3NF by referencing user by ID only. Used to filter notifications for a user.
- `actor_id`
  > [Notification actor] - Implements the requirement to specify who triggered the notification action.
  >
  > Optionally references the user who caused the notification (e.g., someone who replied/liked/reported). Optional for system-generated notifications.
- `post_id`
  > [Related post] - Provides linkage to the post related to the notification, e.g., reply/like events.
  >
  > Referential integrity ensures 3NF and atomicity. For example, when a post is liked.
- `comment_id`
  > [Related comment] - Optionally links to the comment related to the notification.
  >
  > Atomic linkage per notification (never multiple at once). Maintains normalization.
- `report_id`
  > [Related report] - Optionally links this notification to a user report, such as a moderator's response.
  >
  > Ensures traceability for moderation workflows. Maintains normalization.
- `notification_type`
  > [Notification type] - Implements requirement for type-specific notification handling.
  >
  > Defines what kind of notification this is (e.g., 'reply', 'like', 'mention', 'report_resolved', 'system_message'). Follows atomic value requirement for normalization. For example, 'reply' if someone replied to your post.
- `content`
  > [Notification message content] - Implements requirement to inform the user in context.
  >
  > Stores the localized/user-facing message. 3NF ensured as all content is atomic and directly mapped to the notification.
- `is_read`
  > [Read status] - Implements requirement to track notification visibility for each user.
  >
  > Indicates whether the notification has been marked as read. Normalized per (notification, user) tuple.
- `created_at`
  > [Created at] - Timestamp for when the notification was created.
  >
  > Provides audit and chronological sorting. Required for retention, purging, and notification order.
- `read_at`
  > [Read at timestamp] - When the user marked this notification as read.
  >
  > Null until user reads notification. Enables analytics and notification clearing.

### `discussionboard_notification_setting`

[Notification preference] - Implements the requirement for user-configurable notification settings from Section 7 (Notification system).

Stores each user's preference on which types of notifications they want to receive and how (real-time, email, etc). One row per user per notification type. This allows granular opt-in/out and supports both web and email notification channels.

Maintains 3NF compliance:
- Each setting record is atomic: (user, type, channel)
- No redundant/precalculated data

Example: User disables email notifications for likes, keeps web notifications for replies.

Key relationships: links to user, each notification type is discrete.
Special behaviors: critical system notifications may not be opt-out; enforced in application logic.

Properties as follows:

- `id`
  > [Primary key] - Implements unique identification of each notification setting.
  >
  > Atomic identifier for updating/deleting settings efficiently.
- `user_id`
  > [Setting owner] - Links to user who owns this notification preference.
  >
  > Maintains 3NF by referencing only user ID.
- `notification_type`
  > [Notification type] - Specifies which type this setting applies to (e.g., 'reply', 'like', etc).
  >
  > Atomic and fully normalized. Enforces specific per-type setting.
- `channel`
  > [Notification channel] - Defines the delivery method for this setting (e.g., 'web', 'email', 'sms').
  >
  > Each setting only covers one channel. Maintains normalized design.
- `is_enabled`
  > [Enable/disable] - Toggles this notification type per channel for the user.
  >
  > No transitive dependency: True or false for this row only.
  > Example: Disables email notifications for likes.

### `discussionboard_audit_log`

[Audit Log Table] - This implements requirements from 02_discussionboard_functional_requirements.md (Section 10, Audit & Logging), 03_discussionboard_business_rules_and_user_journeys.md, and 04_discussionboard_user_roles_and_permissions.md relating to full system auditing. 

Records every critical action taken on the system (such as account changes, posts, moderation, bans, settings changes, etc.) for traceability and compliance. Maintains 3NF compliance by only storing atomic data for each log event, referencing users and actors as foreign keys without aggregation or summary fields. For example, used when an admin deletes a post or a moderator issues a ban—each such action creates a discrete log entry with timestamp, actor, and related object/user references.

Key relationships: references users (actors), and potentially affected entities (by uuid). Links to event types and device/session info for forensic investigation.
Special behaviors: Immutable once created—no update allowed; only appended and, optionally, soft deleted via deleted_at.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Primary Key] - Implements unique audit log identification. Ensures each entry is uniquely identifiable and supports normalization by not repeating log information elsewhere.
- `actor_id`: [Action Performer] - Links to discussionboard_user. Captures which user (including moderator/admin) performed the audited action. Ensures normalization by referencing actors by ID, not duplicating profile data. For example, when a moderator bans a user, their actor_id is stored here.
- `action`: [Action Type] - Describes the performed action such as 'delete_post', 'ban_user', 'edit_thread', 'change_settings', etc., directly mapping to system business rules. Normalized as atomic string for each event instance. Not a foreign key; main for filtering and search.
- `target_type`: [Target Entity Type] - Indicates type of the entity affected (e.g., 'post', 'user', 'thread', 'comment', 'setting'). Maintains atomic textual data for normalization (no repeated structure).
- `target_id`: [Target Entity ID] - Optional. References affected entity's id (such as post, user, or comment). Nullable if not applicable. Not a foreign key for normalization; just to identify the affected object generically.
- `metadata`: [Extended Metadata] - Optional JSON-encoded string for arbitrary detail, e.g., old_value, new_value, IP address. Remains atomic/normalized as single field—no denormalization.
- `created_at`: [Timestamp] - When the audited action occurred. Provides temporal context, supports querying, and maintains 3NF compliance.
- `deleted_at`: [Soft Delete Timestamp] - Optional. When present, marks entry as deleted but physically retained, satisfying business retention policy requirements.

### `discussionboard_system_event`

[System Event Log] - Implements audit, analytics, and system monitoring requirements from 02_discussionboard_functional_requirements.md (Section 10), supporting platform diagnostics. 

Captures key events not directly tied to user-initiated actions—such as automated job completion, system errors, scheduled cleanups, and background workflow triggers. Maintains full normalization by using discrete, non-overlapping fields and not aggregating or summarizing outcomes. For example, logs a routine backup, failed job, or batch archival event.

Key relationships: not typically directly foreign-keyed to users but records context such as event type, status, and timing.
Special behaviors: Read-only after creation; soft deletion allowed for retention management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Primary Key] - Unique identifier for system event log entry, ensuring 3NF and auditability.
- `event_type`: [Event Type] - Category of system event (e.g. 'backup', 'error', 'prune', 'stats_flush'). Stores normalized event code string.
- `event_status`: [Status] - State of the event: e.g., 'success', 'error', 'pending'. Normalized string field—no repeated meanings.
- `details`: [Details] - Optional. JSON-encoded extra context such as error messages, job metadata. Maintains normalization as atomic blob.
- `created_at`: [Occurrence Time] - When the event was logged. Maintains normalization and supports time range analytics.
- `deleted_at`: [Soft Delete Timestamp] - Optional. When set, indicates removal from system queries but kept for retention requirements.

### `discussionboard_setting`

[Discussion Board Setting] - This implements configuration management requirements, as evidenced in the requirements document (see "Board & Topic Configuration", "Functional Requirements" section, and referenced in "Admin account management").

Business explanation: Represents configurable settings applicable to the platform or to specific boards, such as features toggles, text limits, moderation rules, or security options. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating atomic configuration options from boards or user roles, allowing settings to evolve without redundancy. For example, an admin can adjust allowed image upload size or enable/disable guest comments for all or particular boards.

Key relationships: Possible future relation to discussionboard_board (via board_id) for board-scoped settings. Current settings can be global (no board) or board-specific.
Special behaviors: Unique constraint for (board_id, key) to avoid duplicate keys per board. Settings are not deleted but soft-deleted for audit trails.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Unique identifier for board setting] - Implements the identification requirement for each setting entry. Ensures normalization by serving as the sole PK. For example, referenced for audit logging and updates.
- `board_id`: [Optional board association] - Implements granularity of settings per board. Nullable; null indicates a global (platform-wide) setting. For example, if board_id set, restricts this setting's effect to that board.
- `key`: [Setting key] - Implements key-value settings, e.g., 'max_post_length', 'allow_guests'. Ensures normalization by having atomic keys. For example, referenced by system to look up value for 'image_upload_size'.
- `value`: [Setting value] - The value of the setting, stored as a string for uniformity. Ensures normalization by keeping data atomic and allowing flexible, typed interpretation in code. For example, 'true', '5000', '20MB'.
- `description`: [Setting description] - Describes the purpose of this setting. Ensures clarity and normalization (no denormalized context). For example, 'Maximum allowed characters in a post'.
- `created_at`: [Creation timestamp] - Implements audit trail requirement. Ensures normalized audit logging. For example, to trace when setting was added.
- `updated_at`: [Last modification timestamp] - For audit/logging, when setting was last changed. 3NF-compliant as no calculated content. For example, system checks for setting changes.
- `deleted_at`: [Soft deletion timestamp] - For logical deletion, implementing audit, not physical removal. 3NF-compliant (atomic). For example, admins may undelete settings.

### `discussionboard_tag`

[Tag Management] - This implements tagging and topic-classification requirements from the requirements document (referenced in 'Search & Navigation', 'Thread & Post Management').

Business explanation: Represents tags available for posts/threads, enabling categorization for searching and filtering. Maintains 3NF by representing each tag as an atomic entity. For example, when users add a 'macroeconomics' tag to a thread to make it discoverable for others interested in the topic.

Key relationships: May be assigned to posts, threads, or topics (via associative/junction tables elsewhere).
Special behaviors: Enforces case-insensitive uniqueness; tags can be enabled/disabled (soft-delete pattern, not removed for audit).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Unique identifier for tag] - Implements identity for each tag. Required for normalization and reference by post/tag relations. For example, audit logs can reference this ID.
- `name`: [Display name of tag] - Implements tag search and assignment. Ensures atomic value; 3NF compliance. For example, 'macroeconomics', 'election-2025'.
- `color`: [Display color(hex)] - Customization for user interface, 3NF ensured. For example, '#FF0000' for a 'hot topic' tag.
- `description`: [Tag description] - Optional, clarifies tag use. Ensures atomic, 3NF. For example, 'General discussions on monetary policy.'
- `enabled`: [Active flag] - Whether tag is assignable. Implements tag management rules. Ensures atomicity. For example, disables tag from user assignment without deletion.
- `created_at`: [Creation timestamp] - Fulfills audit/logging requirements. 3NF compliant; not calculated. For example, admins filter tags by creation date.
- `updated_at`: [Last update timestamp] - For tag updates/audit trail. Not denormalized. For example, tag renaming is tracked.
- `deleted_at`: [Soft deletion timestamp] - Supports undelete/soft-delete. Ensures normalization. For example, disable tag, keep history.

### `discussionboard_search_index`

[Discussion Board Search Index] - Implements the advanced/keyword search requirements ('Search & Navigation', 'Functional Requirements').

Business explanation: Caches/facilitates full-text and fuzzy search for posts/threads/comments/tags in a performant manner. Maintains 3NF by storing only normalized references and atomic fields; NO cached, denormalized or precomputed data (summary views to be handled by materialized views only). For example, this powers quick retrieval when user searches 'fiscal stimulus' or 'climate policy'.

Key relationships: References source type and source id (e.g., post, comment, thread); implemented as generic index for extensibility.
Special behaviors: Indexed string for text search, with GIN/trigram index for fuzzy matching. No summary or statistics, just reference and plain content.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: [Unique search index entry ID] - Implements PK/identity for each search index. Enables normalization and reference tracing. For example, needed for maintenance/audit log.
- `source_type`: [Indexed source type] - Implements extensibility (e.g., 'post','thread','comment','tag'). Ensures all index entries refer to atomic entity type. For example, enables post- and thread-specific searches.
- `source_id`: [Referenced entity ID] - FK to the indexed entity. 3NF-compliant; atomic reference. For example, ties to post/thread being indexed.
- `indexed_text`: [Indexed content] - Implements full-text search storage. Atomic per 3NF. For example, stores plain text from posts/comments for searching.
- `created_at`: [Index creation timestamp] - For maintenance, audit logging, and search freshness. 3NF-compliant; not calculated. For example, enables purging stale entries.

Upon success, triggers notification logic and audit logging, and returns the full thread object. Duplicate, conflicting, or malformed thread creation attempts fail with an appropriate error message. This operation does not create initial posts, which must be sent separately. Usage is coordinated with post creation APIs to build up full threads.
operations.summary: Create a new discussion thread (discussionboard_thread).

requestBody.description: New thread creation data.

operations.specification: Updates an existing discussion thread in the 'discussionboard_thread' table by id. Allows thread creators, moderators, or admins to modify thread metadata (title, status flags, topic, etc.). Only enabled when permitted by role policy, board state, and thread lock/deletion. Changes are audited per compliance requirements. Returns modified thread object or errors for unauthorized/invalid requests.
operations.description:
This API updates thread metadata, such as title, topic, pinned/locked state, in the discussionboard_thread table, referencing by thread id as the path parameter. Only thread creator, moderators, or administrators are allowed to update threads, unless overridden by business rules (e.g., locked, deleted, or archived threads may be read-only). Restricted to editable fields as defined by schema and permission logic. Changes are recorded via an audit log record.

Request integrity checks include thread existence, ownership, editability, board/topic validation, and user ban/role status. On forbidden/ineligible updates, an error is returned. The operation must strictly follow constraints on metadata change and not allow retroactive state changes outside policy. Returns the updated thread object on success.

Overall, this update endpoint complements the thread detail and list APIs by enabling the frontend to support renaming, retagging, or status changes workflow.
operations.summary: Update a specific discussion thread by id (discussionboard_thread).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the thread to update.

requestBody.description: Thread update data (editable fields only).

operations.specification: Deletes a discussion thread by id from 'discussionboard_thread'. Operation marks the thread as deleted (soft delete) per data recoverability/audit requirements. Only thread creators, moderators, or admins may perform genuine delete. References are validated, and business/policy constraints are enforced. Audit logs are recorded for compliance.
operations.description:
This API performs a soft delete on a thread record, identified by the unique id in the path parameter. This fulfills recoverability and retention requirements—thread is marked as deleted but not physically removed. Deletion is only allowed if the user is the owner or holds a moderator/admin role for the relevant board. Special-case board/thread-level locks, retention, or legal holds are enforced before delete proceeds.

Deletion triggers audit log and notification logic, and references to posts/comments under the thread remain intact, but are hidden from standard client queries. Errors returned for not found, forbidden, or conflict on deletion attempts. This operation complements recovery/retention logic and is to be coordinated with post and comment deletion in moderation workflows.
operations.summary: Delete (soft-delete) a discussion thread by id (discussionboard_thread).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the thread to delete.

operations.specification: Retrieves a paginated, searchable, and filterable list of posts in the 'discussionboard_post' table. Accepts filters (thread, author, date, is_edited/deleted, text search) with pagination/sort, supporting both standard thread read and advanced discovery. Excludes soft-deleted items unless permitted. Used for thread detail pages, user histories, and content search.
operations.description:
This API returns a list of posts matching the specified search, filter, and pagination parameters. It is used for thread reading (all posts in a thread), user post histories, or global discovery—for instance, showing all posts containing a keyword. Accepts thread_id, created_by_user_id, is_edited, is_deleted, date ranges, and search queries as filter input. Enforces visibility constraints on soft-deleted, locked, or otherwise restricted posts depending on the role of the calling user.

Sort order (by date, relevance, etc.), page size, and offset are controlled via the request body. Outputs a paginated set of post summary or detail objects as appropriate. When combined with comment and like endpoints, supports social and engagement UI features. Returns only posts viewable to calling user, and omits sensitive/admin data for regular users. Audit logs may track high-volume export requests.
operations.summary: List/filter/search posts (discussionboard_post) with pagination and search.

requestBody.description: Post list search, filtering, sorting, and pagination parameters.

operations.specification: Retrieves the details of a single post from 'discussionboard_post' by its id. For reading post content, metadata, and relations to thread/author/attachments. Handles permission checks: deleted, locked, or hidden posts require additional roles; otherwise, regular users can freely access public posts. Excludes sensitive audit/owner fields from response.
operations.description:
This API returns the details for the post referenced by the path parameter id. Response includes all post fields as per the schema, such as content, author, timestamps, is_edited, and any links to thread or attachments if designed to include them. Permission checks ensure that either regular or elevated roles can view posts: for deleted or hidden posts, only creator/mods/admins may view. Audit logs update sensitive read events as required by platform policy.

Used for thread reading as well as user post history and backends analytics.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single post by id (discussionboard_post).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the post to fetch.

operations.specification: Creates a new post within a thread context, stored in 'discussionboard_post'. Used for user participation in discussions—posting responses or the initial post of a thread. Requires thread_ref, content, author, and other metadata. Validates thread existence, permission to post (locked/archived), enforces content validation, notifies subscribed users. Returns created post object on success.
operations.description:
This API creates a new post in a given thread. Required fields in the request body are thread_id, content, and created_by_user_id (the latter often set by backend session authentication). Optionally supports fields such as attachment metadata and is_edited. The platform enforces content validation (length, forbidden content/patterns), verifies thread is open to posting, and blocks attempts in locked/archived threads. Post creation may trigger notification to thread followers as well as logging events for analytics and compliance.

Upon success, returns full details of the created post. Errors include forbidden, invalid thread, conflict, or malformed content.
operations.summary: Create a new post in a thread (discussionboard_post).

requestBody.description: New post creation data.

operations.specification: Updates an existing post by id in 'discussionboard_post'. Allows editing of post body (content), set is_edited flag, and manage soft-delete/restore/un-delete per moderated business logic. Only authors or moderators/admins may invoke. Triggers audit/compliance log. Returns updated post details on success; returns error for unauthorized/invalid states.
operations.description:
This API updates an existing discussion post, referenced by id in the path. Permitted actions include editing content and particular metadata in accordance with business rules and permission policies (e.g., only post author or moderators/admins may edit). All edits set the is_edited flag, and each edit is captured in the audit log for compliance and rollback. Forbidden, not-found, conflict, or locked/deleted states produce error responses.

Strict edit field validation enforces business rules; fields outside policy or role permissions are rejected. Returns the modified post with all current details on success.
operations.summary: Update a single post by id (discussionboard_post).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the post to update.

requestBody.description: Post update data (editable fields only).

operations.specification: Deletes a post by id in 'discussionboard_post'. Implements soft-delete policy for recovery/audit. Only post authors, moderators, or admins may delete posts except in special cases (e.g., system events). Deletes only if post/thread state allows and business rules are satisfied (e.g., thread not locked, post not final/immutable). Cascade impacts (likes, comments, etc.) may be handled in coordination. Writes audit logs. Returns status or error.
operations.description:
This API soft-deletes a post identified by id, as specified in the path parameter. Role and state-based permission logic enforces that deletion is limited to creators, moderators, and administrators, and that locked/archived threads or posts block deletion. Soft-deletion maintains the post for audit/compliance while hiding it from standard display (deleted_at timestamp is set). Audit log records the action and who performed it.

If post is not found or cannot be deleted due to state/permissions, returns error. Used in moderation workflows and user-initiated post removal. Results in restricted post visibility in subsequent queries; does not cascade to physical deletion or related data loss.
operations.summary: Delete (soft-delete) a single post by id (discussionboard_post).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the post to delete.

operations.specification: Implements PATCH method to retrieve a paginated, filtered list of post attachments. This operation is for users or admins wishing to search, filter, or browse files attached to posts, with support for search parameters such as uploader, post, filename, MIME type, upload date, etc. Pagination, search, and sorting are supported. This endpoint is directly associated with the discussionboard_post_attachment table, which stores atomic metadata for each file attached to a post, keeping file entity handling normalized.
operations.description:
This operation enables users, moderators, or admins to search and filter attachments linked to posts. Typically used for auditing, listing user uploads, or for the front-end gallery/file browser in threads and moderation panels.

Role and permission checks must be enforced depending on user context (regular users can only see non-deleted, visible files for posts they have access to; moderators and administrators have more access). Audit logs should record access to non-personal files.

This operation relies on the 3NF structure of the discussionboard_post_attachment table, which encapsulates all file metadata (filename, mimetype, owner, etc). Business logic must validate filter/search parameters to prevent abuse. Pagination and sorting parameters are mandatory for scalable access.

Errors should include forbidden access, bad request for invalid filters, and pagination range errors. Related APIs may include creating (POST /discussionboard/posts/attachments), updating, or removing attachments, as well as parent discussionboard_post endpoints.
operations.summary: Retrieve a paginated/filterable list of post attachments from discussionboard_post_attachment.

requestBody.description: Search/filter, pagination, and sorting parameters for listing post attachments.

responseBody.description: Paginated result with attachment file metadata objects.

operations.specification: Implements GET method to fetch a single post attachment's metadata and details, based on its unique identifier. Tied directly to the discussionboard_post_attachment table, which is used for file metadata normalization related to post uploads. Ensures atomic retrieval of all attachment details, including uploader, file characteristics, upload time, and deletion status.
operations.description:
This endpoint returns the file's metadata, including filename, mimetype, uploader, file size, serving URL, deletion status, etc. Usage examples include confirming upload details for download, checking file status in moderation or user panels, and displaying file preview info in the UI.

Permission logic must ensure that only authorized users (e.g., the uploader, thread/post owner, or moderators/admins) may access the attachment metadata. Invalid or unauthorized access should raise a proper response (404 or permission denied).

This endpoint draws directly from the discussionboard_post_attachment's unique primary key and normalized structure. Adjacent APIs may be list (PATCH), creation (POST), update (PUT), or delete (DELETE) for attachments.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single post attachment's metadata (discussionboard_post_attachment).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Attachment's unique ID (UUID) to fetch.

responseBody.description: Attachment’s metadata details as stored in discussionboard_post_attachment.

operations.specification: Implements POST method to create a new post attachment record. Users upload files (images, documents) directly associated with a discussion post. Operation creates a row in the discussionboard_post_attachment table storing file metadata and access info. Used for adding new file/image assets to posts.
operations.description:
Allows a user to upload (register) a file attachment for an existing post, storing the file's metadata (filename, mimetype, size, serving URL, uploader, timestamp, etc). Actual file upload handling is managed externally (e.g., to S3) and only the metadata is persisted here.

Input validation must include file size/type limits (as configured on the board), checking post existence and user rights to upload, and potential moderation checks for restricted types. This operation enforces normalization by not duplicating file blobs in posts, storing only references.

Failure cases include permission denied, validation errors (invalid type/oversized file), and post not found. Must log actions for audit/context. Related endpoints: PATCH (list attachments), GET (fetch metadata), PUT (update), DELETE (remove file record).
operations.summary: Create a new post attachment (discussionboard_post_attachment).

requestBody.description: Attachment metadata and upload reference info. Includes post_id, filename, URL, uploader, etc.

operations.specification: Implements PUT method to update existing attachment metadata. Only allowed for the uploader, post author, or a moderator/admin for security/compliance. Tied to the discussionboard_post_attachment table and supports changes to fields like filename, mimetype, or is_deleted status.
operations.description:
Used to update metadata for an attachment, e.g., renaming, correcting mimetype, toggling deletion status, or reissuing download URL. Validations must ensure only allowed fields are updated, file remains linked to a valid post, and user/role is permitted to edit. Action is logged for audit.

Disallowed operations are forbidden (such as changing irreversible fields, or operating on soft-deleted records unless by admin). Input is strictly validated according to table schema and business rules. Related endpoints include GET (detail), PATCH (list), POST (create), DELETE (delete file record).
operations.summary: Update metadata/details of a post attachment (discussionboard_post_attachment).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique attachment ID (UUID) to update.

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the attachment record.

responseBody.description: Updated file attachment metadata as stored in discussionboard_post_attachment.

operations.specification: Implements DELETE method to soft-delete a file attachment associated with a post, corresponding to a row in the discussionboard_post_attachment table. Operation marks file as deleted, does not physically remove records for audit/data recovery compliance.
operations.description:
This logically deletes the file attachment so it is no longer shown to regular users but remains retrievable for audit and recovery by moderators/admins. Standard permission logic must ensure only uploader, post owner, or moderator/admin can delete the record. Edge cases, such as removing already deleted records or forbidden access, must be handled. Audit must log all delete operations.

Underpins data compliance by not physically dropping potentially sensitive or important file records. Rollback/recovery policies should reference the deleted_at timestamp. Related operations: POST (add attachment), PUT (edit), GET (single record), PATCH (list).
operations.summary: Delete/soft-delete a post attachment (discussionboard_post_attachment).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the attachment to delete (UUID).

responseBody.description: Result/confirmation of deletion, or metadata of the soft-deleted attachment.

operations.specification: Implements PATCH operation for searching/listing comments. This endpoint allows all users (with privacy/visibility/authorization enforcement) to search, paginate, and filter comments linked to posts, with support for searching by author, post, parent, content, creation date, or deletion status. Underlying table: discussionboard_comment. Output is always paginated and sorted. Complies with list/search pattern in modern API practice.
operations.description:
Allows retrieval/search of comments associated with posts (and optionally threaded). Use cases include thread/post discussion views, moderation panels, or personal comment history. Only visible comments are shown to regular users (filter on is_deleted, permissions), while mods/admins can see all.

Search parameters allow filtering by post, user, parent comment, keywords, etc., and support UI-driven comment browsing and search. Result always paginated. Security checks must prevent unauthorized access to non-public comments, and ensure searches are not abused for scraping or threat models.

Errors include permission denied, invalid search parameter, out-of-range pagination. Useful complements: GET (fetch single comment), POST (create), PUT (edit), DELETE (remove/restore).
operations.summary: Paginated, filtered list of comments from discussionboard_comment.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination options for fetching comments.

operations.specification: Implements GET method for fetching a single comment, based on unique comment id. Directly tied to the discussionboard_comment table (normalized, atomic record). Used for retrieving all attributes (author, content, creation/modification/parent, status, etc) of one comment identified by primary key. Matches standard detail-retrieval API design.
operations.description:
Used in comment detail views, moderation tools, or post/comment management UI to view the full record of an individual comment. Enforces access controls (normal users can only see non-deleted/authorized comments; mods/admins may see all, including hidden/removed).

The endpoint looks up and returns the comment using its normalized primary key, as per discussionboard_comment schema. Permission errors, not found, or access to private/deleted comments are handled with appropriate error codes.
operations.summary: Retrieve a single post comment (discussionboard_comment) by ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique comment ID (UUID) to retrieve.

responseBody.description: Full detail about the requested comment.

operations.specification: Implements POST operation for creating a new comment for a post (or as a threaded reply to another comment, one level deep). Maps directly to the discussionboard_comment table, which enforces 3NF for comment entities. This enables independent record-keeping for each comment—use for reply composition or post discussion addition.
operations.description:
Enables users to create and store a new comment entity for a given post, either as a top-level comment or as a threaded reply to another comment (1-level deep threading via parent_comment_id). All required validation (content length, parent linkage, permissions, anti-spam) enforced as per business rules. Input is atomic: post_id, created_by_user_id, content, and optional parent. Returns full record for UI or further processing.

Audit logging required; abuse/spam risks mitigated with content validation and appropriate throttling. Related endpoints: PATCH (list/search), GET (detail), PUT (edit), DELETE (soft-delete/restore).
operations.summary: Create a new comment for a post (discussionboard_comment).

requestBody.description: Fields for creating a comment (post, content, user, parent, etc).

operations.specification: Implements PUT operation for updating content/attributes of an existing comment (discussionboard_comment). Only the author, moderators, or admins can update. Used for editing comment text, marking as edited, or handling restored/undeleted status. Table is normalized and only metadata fields change.
operations.description:
Used to modify a comment (e.g., update content, correct parent, or change is_edited flag as per editing workflow). Input values are validated for allowed edits by user/role and logic (e.g., can't set arbitrary parent, can't remove moderation flags as regular user). Action logged for full audit/compliance as per requirements.

Forbidden changes return errors (e.g. unauthorized, immutable fields, modifying a deleted comment). Supports comment editing UI and standard moderation tools. Use together with GET (detail), PATCH (list), POST (create), DELETE (remove/restore).
operations.summary: Update attributes/content for a post comment (discussionboard_comment).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique comment ID (UUID) to update.

requestBody.description: Fields which may be edited/updated for the comment.

operations.specification: Implements DELETE operation for soft-deleting a comment in the discussionboard_comment table. Removes from UI display for most users but preserves for audit, mod/admin, and possible recovery. Compliance with logical-delete business rules. Only author, moderators, or admins may delete.
operations.description:
Marks the comment as is_deleted with a deletion timestamp, without physically removing. Only permitted users (author, mod, admin) may delete. Handles forbidden, already deleted, or not found records with standard errors and records all actions in audit log.

Supports moderation and compliance requirements for reversible comment removal, content flagging, and anti-abuse handling. Complements POST (add comment), PUT (edit), GET (detail), PATCH (list/search).
operations.summary: Soft-delete (logically remove) a comment from posts (discussionboard_comment).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Comment's unique ID (UUID) to remove.

operations.specification: Implements PATCH method to search and paginate likes on posts or comments (discussionboard_likes table, 3NF atomic representation). For use by front-end to display recent likes, moderation analytics, or audit panels. Filtering by content (post, comment), liking user, or timestamp, with pagination and search. No editing/creation via this endpoint.
operations.description:
Enables clients to retrieve a paginated and filtered list of 'like' records, supporting analytics, display of who liked a post/comment, or for moderation history. Typical filters: by user, post, comment, or date. Pagination and sorting enforced for efficient large-set handling.

Output population matches atomic rows from discussionboard_likes. Access controls must ensure only authorized data is viewed (e.g., limit user-to-user cross-viewing in privacy context). Useful alongside endpoints for liking/unliking content (POST/DELETE not defined here), and for analytics/reporting. Errors include out-of-range pagination or forbidden filters.
operations.summary: List/search paginated like events on post/comment (discussionboard_likes).

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination for likes.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of likes as atomic records from discussionboard_likes.

operations.specification: Implements GET operation for retrieving the full detail of a 'like' event (discussionboard_likes) by its primary key (UUID). Used to display all metadata about the 'like' (user, post/comment, timestamp). Direct mapping to normalized DB table.
operations.description:
Fetches all details for a single like event, as used by moderation tools, reporting panels, or engagement analytics. Role checks are crucial (users see only their own likes, mods/admins may be broader). Access to metadata, not content.

Usually used together with PATCH (search/list), or analytic endpoints. Includes error handling for forbidden/missing records.
operations.summary: Get a single like event by its ID (discussionboard_likes).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique like ID (UUID) to fetch.

responseBody.description: Full like event metadata from discussionboard_likes.

operations.specification: Create a new like record, representing when a user performs a like action on a post or comment. This operation corresponds to the discussionboard_likes table in the Prisma schema. The like event is atomic, meaning each like can belong to either a post or comment, but not both. The operation requires user authentication and ensures only permitted users can like content. On creation, it records the user, and either the post or comment target, with the created_at timestamp. Uniqueness is enforced for (user_id, post_id) and (user_id, comment_id) pairs. Related use cases include toggling likes, retrieving like history, and preventing duplicate likes.
operations.description: This endpoint allows a user to like a post or comment. According to the discussionboard_likes schema, the operation will require the authenticated user's identity, and a target post or comment UUID as input. On creation, it must ensure uniqueness for the (user_id, post_id) or (user_id, comment_id) pair to prevent duplicate likes and set the created_at timestamp. The operation should reject attempts to like both a post and comment simultaneously or neither. Only authenticated users can use this endpoint; attempts without proper authentication must be refused. If a like already exists, the API should return an appropriate conflict error. On success, the endpoint returns the created like entity, including like id and target details.
operations.summary: Create a new like record (discussionboard_likes table).

requestBody.description: Like creation payload. Must provide either post_id or comment_id (but not both).

operations.specification: Update an existing like record identified by its unique ID. This works with the discussionboard_likes table in the Prisma schema. The operation allows users to alter details of their like record, such as changing the target post or comment (though typical use is limited). Permissions should ensure only the user who created the like can update it. It must enforce mutual exclusivity of post_id and comment_id. Audit timestamps and modification integrity are ensured.
operations.description: This endpoint updates an existing like record, given its unique ID. According to the schema, a like can refer to either a post or a comment, but not both at once. On update, the system performs validation to avoid conflicting targets. Only the owner of the like can perform the update. The endpoint responds with the updated like record. Attempts to update with invalid target or by unauthorized users are rejected with appropriate error codes. Proper request and response typing are referenced from IDiscussionboardLike interfaces.
operations.summary: Update a like record by ID (discussionboard_likes table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the like record to update.

requestBody.description: Like update payload. Must maintain mutual exclusivity between post_id and comment_id.

operations.specification: Delete a like record by its unique ID, as per the discussionboard_likes table in the Prisma schema. This operation allows a user to remove their like from a post or comment. Only the user who created the like can delete it. Removal will make the user able to like the same content again. Ensures audit-ability and enforces appropriate authentication and authorization.
operations.description: This endpoint deletes a like record given its UUID. Only the user who created the like is authorized to perform this deletion. Attempts by other users must be rejected. Upon success, the like is fully removed, allowing the user to like the same post or comment again in the future. Attempts to delete a non-existent like should yield a not found response.
operations.summary: Delete a like record by ID (discussionboard_likes table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the like record to delete.

responseBody.description: Deletion confirmation result, or null if resource was not found.

operations.specification: Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of bookmarks for the authenticated user from the discussionboard_bookmarks table. Allows searching and filtering by post ID, creation date, or sorting preferences. The endpoint supports advanced queries and pagination to handle large bookmark histories. Only the bookmarks belonging to the user are visible.
operations.description: This endpoint provides a list retrieval with filters and pagination for bookmarks in the discussionboard_bookmarks table. Query parameters may supply searching by post, date range, or sorting by creation date. The operation is only available to authenticated users and only exposes bookmarks owned by the user. The response includes paginated data following IPageIDiscussionboardBookmark typing. Error handling includes overlimit queries, unauthorized access, and invalid filter combinations.
operations.summary: List and search user bookmarks (discussionboard_bookmarks table).

requestBody.description: Request object for searching, filtering, and paginating bookmarks.

operations.specification: Retrieve a specific bookmark record via its unique ID from the discussionboard_bookmarks table. Used for inspecting a single bookmarked post for the authenticated user. Enforces proper ownership and authorization.
operations.description: This endpoint retrieves a single bookmark record using its UUID. Only the user who owns the bookmark record is authorized to retrieve it. The response includes all bookmark details as described in IDiscussionboardBookmark. If the bookmark does not exist or is owned by another user, the request fails with not found or forbidden errors, respectively.
operations.summary: Get bookmark record by ID (discussionboard_bookmarks table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the bookmark record to retrieve.

operations.specification: Create a new bookmark for a post in the discussionboard_bookmarks table. Each user can only bookmark a post once. The bookmark enables users to save posts for later retrieval. On creation, uniqueness for (user_id, post_id) is enforced. Returns full bookmark entity on success.
operations.description: This endpoint adds a bookmark to a post on behalf of the authenticated user. The payload requires the post_id of the post to be bookmarked. Each user can bookmark a specific post only once; attempts to duplicate will result in a conflict error. Only authenticated users are permitted. On success, the operation returns details of the created bookmark entity.
operations.summary: Create a new bookmark for a post (discussionboard_bookmarks table).

requestBody.description: Bookmark creation payload with post_id.

operations.specification: Update an existing bookmark record identified by its unique ID, in the discussionboard_bookmarks table. Allows users to modify their bookmarks, such as updating metadata (if applicable in the schema). Only the owner may perform the operation. Completes audit and integrity requirements.
operations.description: This endpoint allows a user to update their bookmark record by ID. The main updatable field is typically metadata or context, as the post_id should remain immutable after creation. Validation should ensure only owners can update and that required fields are provided. On success, returns the updated bookmark record, or appropriate errors if forbidden or not found.
operations.summary: Update a bookmark record by ID (discussionboard_bookmarks table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the bookmark record to update.

requestBody.description: Bookmark update payload (fields per schema).

operations.specification: Delete a bookmark record by its unique ID. Refers to the discussionboard_bookmarks table. Removes a user's bookmark from a post, allowing them to re-bookmark it later if they wish. Only the bookmark owner can delete the record.
operations.description: This endpoint deletes a specific bookmark, given its ID. The user must be authenticated and must own the bookmark to delete it. Upon successful deletion, the resource is removed and the bookmark can be recreated in the future. If the ID does not match a bookmark owned by the user, an error is returned.
operations.summary: Delete a bookmark by ID (discussionboard_bookmarks table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the bookmark record to delete.

responseBody.description: Deletion confirmation result, or null if resource was not found.

operations.specification: Retrieve a paginated and searchable list of follow relationships from the discussionboard_follows table for the authenticated user. Enables users to view others they follow (users or threads), with optional filters and sorts. Restricts access to the account owner or privileged admin (future vision).
operations.description: This endpoint lists the user's current follow relationships, possibly filtered by followed user, thread, or creation date, with support for pagination and sorting. The request body defines the search and pagination criteria. Only follow records the user owns are returned. Possible errors include overlimit or invalid request format. Typical use cases are rendering followed thread/user lists, or synchronizing user preferences.
operations.summary: List/search user follows (discussionboard_follows table).

requestBody.description: Follow search and pagination request object.

responseBody.description: Paginated response object containing follows data.

operations.specification: Retrieve a specific follow relationship by its unique ID from the discussionboard_follows table. Supports user inspecting a single follow record by its unique id, enforcing ownership or admin privilege. Used to resolve follow record details or as part of follow management UIs.
operations.description: Retrieves a single follow entity given its unique UUID. Only the owner or an admin (future extensibility) can view the record. Returns all fields as per IDiscussionboardFollow, or appropriate error if not found or forbidden.
operations.summary: Get a follow record by ID (discussionboard_follows table).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the follow record to retrieve.

operations.specification: Create a new follow relationship in the discussionboard_follows table, enabling a user to follow either another user or a thread. Each (follower_user_id, followed_user_id) or (follower_user_id, followed_thread_id) pair is unique, preventing duplicate follows. User can only follow one target per event. Authentication is required.
operations.description: Creates a new follow record, provided with either a followed_user_id or a followed_thread_id (not both). Request is rejected if the pair already exists. Only authenticated users are eligible. Creation sets the created_at timestamp and returns the new follow entity with all details.
operations.summary: Create a new follow (discussionboard_follows table).

This endpoint enables administrators and moderators to retrieve a searchable, paginated, and sortable list of all moderation actions recorded in the discussion board system. Each moderation action documents an intervention by a moderator or admin—such as edit, hide, delete, warn, ban, or restore—providing a full audit trail of moderation activities. 

Access to this endpoint is typically restricted to users with administrative or moderation permissions, due to the sensitive nature of moderation data. The results include references to the acting moderator/admin, affected users, posts/comments, and related reports. Filters should allow querying by action type, actor, time range, target type, or related entity, in alignment with moderation reporting requirements.

This operation supports advanced audit compliance and transparency by delivering precise, atomic details of each moderation event. It can be used together with GET /discussionboard/moderationActions/{id} to drill down to a specific action. Pagination and complex filtering are required due to the potentially high volume of moderation actions.

The information returned includes which moderator or admin performed the action, the action type (e.g., edit, delete, ban), any associated user, post, comment, or report, the moderation reason, and the action timestamp.

Permissions are typically restricted to moderation or administrative users to preserve the privacy and security of moderation workflows. The endpoint is essential for investigating individual incidents in depth, conducting audits, and assuring traceability. It complements the moderation action search/list endpoint, enabling users to drill down into specific events for further review or compliance verification.

operations.description: This endpoint searches and lists configuration settings from the 'discussionboard_setting' table. The 'id' field is a UUID primary key, ensuring every setting is uniquely retrievable.

This endpoint does not expose or modify mutable settings data, ensuring read-only access aligned with the principle of least privilege. Request authorization may restrict this endpoint to admin or privileged user roles. When a setting is not found, appropriate error handling and status codes must be returned. Filtering can be based on tag name, enabled/disabled state, or other tag metadata such as description. Pagination, sorting, and fuzzy search are typically supported in the PATCH request body schema (IDiscussionboardTag.IRequest). Responses include a paged container of tag objects, as defined by IPageIDiscussionboardTag.

Admins and advanced users may use this endpoint for tag management and bulk review. Soft-deleted tags (as indicated by the deleted_at column) may be included or excluded based on system settings. Search operations may enable case-insensitive and partial matches using trigram indexes. Proper authorization should protect this endpoint, with permissions granularity enforced by role.

Typical use cases include displaying tag details, editing interfaces, or checking tag status for assignment. The endpoint returns all non-sensitive properties, such as tag name, color, description, and enabled state.

If the tag entry is missing or soft-deleted, an appropriate error is returned, consistent with platform error handling policy. This is a read-only operation.

Tag name uniqueness (case-insensitive) is enforced, and updates may be refused if such constraints are violated.

This patch endpoint provides complex querying and batch listing capabilities for the discussionboard_search_index table. The request body schema (IDiscussionboardSearchIndex.IRequest) supports filtering by source_type, source_id, indexed_text, and additional pagination/sorting options. Typical consumers include search administration tools, analytics dashboards, and index management utilities.

This operation is read-only, supporting audit-compliance and analytics. Handles cases where no index entries are available, large result sets, and advanced filtering. Pagination controls, error reporting, and access checks may apply based on sensitivity of indexed content.

This get operation retrieves a discussionboard_search_index entry by ID from the database for display, diagnostics, or troubleshooting. Appropriate for search index management, analytics, or review workflows. The response returns all non-sensitive properties for the indexed entity, including indexed_text, source_type, and timestamps.

Absent or soft-deleted index entries are handled with error responses in compliance with platform conventions. This is a read-only operation for viewing individual search index records.

operations.description:
This API creates a new index entry for the discussionboard_search_index table, representing full-text/cached searchable content for posts, threads, comments, or tags. Used for powering the search engine and search tools. Payload must adhere to IDiscussionboardSearchIndex.ICreate, including type, source_id, and indexed text.

Insertions are usually automated or highly restricted. Validates required fields, enforces allowed source types, and may require authentication as an admin or system agent. The newly created index entry, with timestamps and IDs, is returned upon success, errors handled per business policy.

requestBody.description: Details for the new search index entry.

operations.specification: Implements update operation for the search index record in the discussionboard_search_index table. This endpoint allows an authorized admin to update a search index entry by its unique identifier. It is used for recalculating or repopulating the indexed text, updating the metadata, or correcting any field after identifying stale or incorrect search records (such as those resulting from content edits or restores). Updating search indices is critical for keeping full-text and keyword search results in sync with the actual discussionboard entities (posts, threads, comments, tags). Strict validation must ensure only permitted updates – the ID in the path matches an actual search index entry, and only certain fields may be updated. This operation is audited for analytics and traceability. This endpoint is typically used together with the creation endpoint and may require pre-validation or locking to avoid search result inconsistencies.
operations.description:
This API operation updates an existing search index record in the discussionboard_search_index table by its unique ID. It is typically used by admin users, the background indexer, or trusted system processes to correct, repopulate, or refresh search index entries when their source entity is changed (such as after content editing, tag updates, or thread reclassification). 

Security: Only administrators are permitted to perform this update to prevent accidental corruption of the search index. The update is recorded in the audit logs for compliance and error-tracing.

Schema relationship: The discussionboard_search_index table is normalized to reference the source entity type (post, comment, thread, tag) and ID, along with the indexed textual content. Updating this record recalculates its indexed_text or, if required, repairs a broken reference.

Validation: The operation must ensure the validity of new indexed_text and retain referential integrity to the referenced entity. Application logic must guard against race conditions, especially during concurrent search updates. 

Related endpoints: The creation (POST) and deletion (DELETE) endpoints for search indices typically accompany this update. Error handling must clarify if the specified ID does not exist or if attempted fields cannot be changed (immutable fields should not be altered).

Expected behavior: Success returns the updated search index entity; errors include not found, forbidden, or validation failures. On update, the search engine may need to be notified to refresh indexes.
operations.summary: Update a specific search index record in the discussionboard_search_index table.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the search index record to update.

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the search index entry, such as indexed_text, source_type, and source_id.

responseBody.description: The updated search index record after applying modifications.

operations.specification: Implements deletion operation for a search index record in the discussionboard_search_index table. This endpoint allows an authorized admin to remove a search index entry by its unique identifier. Used when the source entity is deleted, purged, or needs to be excluded from search results, ensuring that orphaned or outdated index entries do not persist and degrade search accuracy. The deletion is soft or hard depending on the internal rules and audit/compliance needs. Critical for search result integrity, performance, and audit. Deleting a search index may trigger downstream effects on search cache/materialized views. This API must prevent unintended cascade deletions or internal corruption – it will not touch the original source entity. Operation is fully auditable and must be restricted to privileged users or system tasks. Often paired with content deletion endpoints or routine maintenance jobs.
operations.description:
Deletes a search index record by its unique ID from the discussionboard_search_index table. This is used by admins or system maintenance processes to remove search entries that are no longer valid (for example, after a post, comment, or thread has been deleted, or when an index entry is discovered to be stale or erroneous).

Security: Only those with admin-level authorization are permitted to invoke this endpoint, as it can affect user-facing search experiences and overall data integrity. The operation is logged in audit systems for traceability.

Relationship to schema: The search index record being deleted contains references to the source entity (type and ID), as well as its indexed content. Deletion does not cascade to the source entity – only the index entry is removed.

Validation: The API checks if the specified search index ID exists. Attempting to delete a non-existent index should clearly indicate the failure reason. Access is strictly checked; only admins may invoke this.

Related endpoints: Used together with the creation (POST) and update (PUT) endpoints for search indices. Upon deletion, search caches may need invalidation, and analytics systems updated accordingly.

Expected outcome: On success, confirm removal (or soft deletion, per policy). Errors include "not found", "forbidden", or internal system errors. The result is usually a status payload or the deleted record's metadata for audit.
operations.summary: Delete a specific search index record in the discussionboard_search_index table.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the search index record to delete.

responseBody.description: A confirmation payload or metadata about the deleted search index record.

IDiscussionboardUser.IRequest.description:
유저 검색 및 목록 조회 요청 DTO.

필터링, 페이징, 정렬 옵션을 포함한다. 이메일/닉네임/활성상태 등을 기반으로 검색할 때 사용한다.

Prisma discussionboard_user 모델의 관리용 검색 조건과 3NF 준수 설계 참고.

displayName.description: 닉네임 기반 검색. 사용자의 표시 이름(글쓴이 란 등에서 보임, 부분일치/완전일치 검색 지원). Prisma: display_name 컬럼. 예시: '정치매니아'

email.description: 이메일 주소로 검색. 로그인/고유 식별 목적. Prisma: email 컬럼. 예시: 'user@example.com'

isActive.description: 활성화 상태(계정 유효/잠금 등)을 기준으로 필터링. Prisma: is_active 컬럼.

isBanned.description: 전체 플랫폼 벤 여부로 필터. Prisma: is_banned 컬럼.

registeredFrom.description: 가입일 시작(이 이후 가입한 유저 조회). Prisma: created_at 컬럼. ISO8601 datetime 사용.

registeredTo.description: 가입일 종료(이전에 가입한 유저 조회). Prisma: created_at 컬럼. ISO8601 datetime 사용.

sort.description: 정렬 필드. 예: 'created_at desc', 'display_name asc' 등. 지원 필드는 쿼리 사양에 참고, 사용자가 선택.

page.description: 요청 페이지 번호. 1부터 시작.

limit.description: 페이지당 결과 수. 시스템 기본값/최대값 참고. (ex: 50, 100 등)

cursor.description: 커서 기반 페이지네이션을 사용할 때 이전 페이지의 마지막 ID 등.

IPageDiscussionboardUser.ISummary.description:
유저 목록 요약형 페이지 컨테이너.

discussionboard_user 요약 DTO 리스트와 페이지 메타 정보를 포함한다.

Prisma discussionboard_user 테이블에서 제공하는 최소한의 주요 필드만 응답함.

3NF 데이터베이스 설계, API 표준 Pagination 구조 참고.

data.description: 유저 요약 리스트.

current.description:
현재 페이지 번호입니다. 1부터 시작하며, 클라이언트가 페이징 네비게이션을 구현할 때 사용됩니다.

페이지 기반 API에서 필수적으로 사용되는 메타 정보로, 서버가 반환하는 페이지의 실제 번호입니다.

limit.description:
페이지마다 최대 몇 개의 레코드를 반환할지 나타냅니다.

많은 API에서 100을 기본값으로 하지만, 클라이언트에서 요청 시 바꿀 수 있으며 최대 제한은 비즈니스 로직에서 관리합니다. 체계적인 데이터 노출과 네트워크 효율을 위해 필요합니다.

records.description:
전체 데이터베이스 기준으로 검색된 레코드의 총 개수입니다. 페이징 UI, 페이지 갯수 계산 등에 활용합니다.

API 응답이 페이징될 때, 전체 피드 또는 목록에 몇 개의 결과가 있는지 제공하는 핵심적인 메타정보입니다.

pages.description:
전체 페이지의 총 개수입니다.

records/limit의 올림(ceiling) 값으로 산정합니다(0.1 페이지도 하나의 페이지로 처리해야 하기 때문입니다). 클라이언트에서 마지막 네비게이션 버튼, 범위 체크 등에 활용됩니다.

IPage.IPagination.description: 페이지 정보. 레코드 리스트에 대한 페이징 메타데이터로, 클라이언트의 UI 페이징, 네비게이션, 전체 범위 계산 등에 사용됩니다.

IDiscussionboardUser.ICreate.description:
유저 신규 생성(회원가입) API 요청 DTO.

이메일, 비밀번호(해시), 닉네임, 아바타 등 회원 정보 입력. 유니크 필드/필수/옵션 명확히 구분.

관리자 추가, 일반 회원가입 모두 대응. password_hash 필드는 API 입력 단계에서는 실비밀번호가 아니라 API 내부 해시됨.

password.description: 사용자 원시 패스워드(입력 전송 시만 보류, 저장은 hash 후). 절대 API 응답에 노출 X.

isActive.description: 계정 활성화 여부. 기본 true; 관리자용 생성시 비활성 가능(옵션). Prisma: is_active

IDiscussionboardUser.IUpdate.description:
유저 전체 정보 변경(일괄 수정/PUT) API 요청 DTO.

비밀번호와 같이 인증 구간에서만 교체되는 필드는 별도 password_change API분리 권장.

email.description: 새 이메일. 시스템 전체에서 고유해야 함. Prisma: email

isBanned.description: 플랫폼 차단 메뉴얼 조작. Prisma: is_banned.

1:1 discussionboard_user_profile 주요/핵심 필드만 포함. ex) 프로필 ID, user_id, bio 등 핵심값 중심. DB 3NF/개별 관리.

운영 대시보드 등에서 대량 노출 시 데이터 절약 및 성능 개선용 설계.

수정일(최종 업데이트 타임스탬프)는 서버단 자동 처리.

archived_at.description:
Timestamp recording when the board archive snapshot was taken.

Follows ISO 8601 date-time format. This is the immutable event time for compliance/audit purposes.

name_snapshot.description:
The board's display name as of the archive's creation.

Captured for rollback, compliance, or reactivation workflows.

description_snapshot.description:
The board's full description field as of the archived snapshot.

Used for preview/restoration and historical analysis.

slug_snapshot.description: The board's slug (URL-safe segment) as of the archive, for navigation and record linkage.

IDiscussionboardBoardArchive.description:
A complete board archive snapshot entry. Represents a historical record of all display and reference fields for a board at the moment it was archived, as well as archival agent and timestamp.

Strictly immutable after initial creation, used for full rollback and compliance/audit logics.

board_id.description:
Filter: Only threads for the specified board (board_id).

Used when retrieving all threads within a particular discussion board for content feeds or navigation.

oneOf.description:
Filter: Only threads associated with the given topic ID.

Nullable. When set, restricts results to threads belonging to a particular board-level topic.

topic_id.description:
Filter: Only threads associated with the given topic ID.

Nullable. When set, restricts results to threads belonging to a particular board-level topic.

oneOf.description:
Filter: Only threads created by the user with the given UUID.

Supports finding all threads authored by a particular user.

created_by_user_id.description:
Filter: Only threads created by the user with the given UUID.

Supports finding all threads authored by a particular user.

oneOf.description:
Filter: Only threads marked as pinned (important/announcement etc).

Nullable, enabling filter for pinned or non-pinned threads.

is_pinned.description:
Filter: Only threads marked as pinned (important/announcement etc).

Nullable, enabling filter for pinned or non-pinned threads.

oneOf.description:
Filter: Only threads locked for posting (true) or unlocked (false).

Optional. Used for moderation workflows and UX filtering.

is_locked.description:
Filter: Only threads locked for posting (true) or unlocked (false).

Optional. Used for moderation workflows and UX filtering.

oneOf.description:
Filter: Only soft-deleted threads (true), only active (false), or all (null).

Moderators/admins can retrieve deleted content, regular users only active.

is_deleted.description:
Filter: Only soft-deleted threads (true), only active (false), or all (null).

Moderators/admins can retrieve deleted content, regular users only active.

oneOf.description: Filter: Only threads created after this datetime (ISO8601).

min_created_at.description: Filter: Only threads created after this datetime (ISO8601).

oneOf.description: Filter: Only threads created before this datetime (ISO8601).

max_created_at.description: Filter: Only threads created before this datetime (ISO8601).
